# Appeal of Denial — Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)

**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026, effective 2026-08-04
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

**Member:** Emerson Alvarez
**Member ID:** W977514824
**Denial date:** 2026-08-09
**Reference number:** POC-4E415360FE-32022

---

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130). My denial notice, dated 2026-08-09, states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision because the medical records already in my file address the specific elements the plan's own policy requires. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me.

## The plan's criteria and how my records address them

Cigna's policy states that hip replacement is medically necessary "for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met." Among the required elements are documentation of function-limiting pain, loss of hip function, and failure of (or a documented reason to forgo) provider-directed non-surgical management. My records contain all of this:

**Function-limiting pain.** The policy requires:

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

My records show 24 months of progressive hip pain, and that I now ambulate with a cane and am limited to walking one block. This is well beyond the three-month duration the policy describes, and it meets the distance/functional description in the plan's own language.

**Loss of function affecting daily activities.** The policy requires:

> "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records document that I cannot put on my shoes unassisted, which is a basic activity of daily living.

**Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management.** The policy requires:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My records show 16 weeks (2026-03-03 to 2026-06-23, 20 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, four months of NSAID use with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-15 that gave only three weeks of partial relief. This is documented, provider-directed conservative treatment that lasted well over the three months the policy describes, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

The policy also allows an exception when the record documents why continued non-surgical management is not appropriate:

> "The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate."

Between the extended trial of therapy, medication, and injection already completed, and the imaging findings on 2026-06-02 (weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph showing joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes), my chart shows both that conservative management was tried and that it did not resolve the underlying joint changes.

## What I am asking

I am asking Cigna to review this appeal together with the complete clinical record — including the physical therapy discharge note, the imaging report from 2026-06-02, and my surgeon's documentation — and to reconsider the determination that the documentation was incomplete. If any specific piece of documentation is still needed, I would appreciate a clear, specific list of what is missing so that my surgeon's office and I can provide it promptly.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. I am submitting it by logging in at my.cigna.com to use the plan's appeal form, and/or by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member ID card. I am using the appeal address printed on my denial letter for any mailed copy of this appeal.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Emerson Alvarez
Member ID: W977514824
Date: [date of signing]
Contact phone/email: [patient contact information]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
